text: {"frames":["You lift the lamp in the corridor and the lady in the portrait has turned her head. Yesterday she held her fan high, and now she holds it low. A thread of wool hangs from her sleeve, and it trails down to the floor. Beside her hangs a clock with a bright face. What time does the clock in the picture show?","The stairs go up past the last floor on the plan, and at the top the bell rope has vanished. Femke searches the landing twice and finds only a wet footprint on the boards. A door stands open where no door should be, and a cold smell of wet wood drifts out. Somewhere a clock ticks slowly behind the wall. What time does the clock in the picture show?","A map has appeared on the door of the lowest floor, drawn in green thread and pinned with a tiny brass button. Anke knocks and a small voice on the other side begs for help. The map does not show the way out, only a clock with its hands drawn in the corner. Lot wants to know if the clock was right. What time does the clock in the picture show?","A smell of hot wax drifts down the stairs, and a blue light glows through the mill window. You follow it to the barge tied at the bottom of the canal, where a lantern burns blue above the water. The lantern rocks, and the bell on the mast gives a soft ring. Bas points at the round clock painted on the bulkhead, the only thing on the barge that still keeps time. What time does the clock in the picture show?","Yesterday the canal ran to the town, but this morning the water flows the other way, back into the forest. The ducks drift upstream, and the lock gate groans as if it wants to shut. Joop stands on the bridge with a wet clog in his hand and a clock sign on the lock house wall. Nobody knows when the water turned around. What time does the clock in the picture show?"]}
